Done. PR 131's description and trail 91 both corrected.

## What changed

**PR body** — surgical replacement of the "The fix" section only. The diff removed 4 lines and rewrote them in place; the other ~730 lines of the body are byte-identical, which I verified before publishing.

The section now describes three layers instead of two, and is explicit that:
- `validateRef` rejects NUL and refspec syntax but **not** a leading `-`, that `d7b3880a` removed that rule deliberately, and why — a shape check refuses valid refs like `refs/tags/-foo` and `refs/heads/-release`
- `--end-of-options` does **not** cover `clone --branch <ref>`, which sits before it; that slot is safe for the separate reason that git takes `--branch`'s value literally, with the verified output
- remote resolution is what lets layer 1 stop rejecting by shape
- **"no network call added" was wrong and is withdrawn** — `remoteRefFor` runs `ls-remote` for hex/`+`/`-` refs

**Trail 91** was worse than the PR body and I'd have missed it if I hadn't checked. It still asserted the **withdrawn code-execution claim** — *"would execute an arbitrary command during the fetch operation… enabling code execution on the benchmarking system"* — which the author verified is unreachable over https, and which the PR body retracted rounds ago. A reader triaging by trail alone would have rated this critical. It now leads with the corrected severity (silently wrong checkout, not code execution), says plainly that the earlier claim is withdrawn and why, and carries the three-layer design plus the full verification record.

No commit, no push — `d7b3880a` is untouched, so CI doesn't re-run and the existing green stays valid.

# RFD 0004 - Converge code search on one engine, deprecate duplicates

Status: Proposed (RFC, open for comment). P2.M1, COR-786
Date: 2026-08-21

## TLDR

We maintain two independent tree-sitter extractor stacks and have no single front door for code
search. This RFD proposes **Option A**: entire-graph becomes the precision symbol **producer**,
emitting a SCIP index per `repo@commit` that peregrine ingests into its already-reserved
`SymbolSource::Scip` / `SymbolPrecision::Semantic` slots. peregrine stays the find-text-fast
**serving** engine and the single front door. entire-graph stays the understand-structure engine
(relations, impact, brain). Each retires its duplicate half: peregrine stops owning symbol
precision, entire-graph stops building a search engine.

Embedding backbone consolidation is **not** in scope. That is COR-788 and gets its own RFD.

## Context

### The honest inventory

| System | Owner | Lang | Role today | Backbone | Deployed? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **peregrine** | Evis | Rust | Lexical code search: trigram index, regex, symbol/fuzzy search, cross-file go-to-def | Trigram postings (Roaring), zstd content. No vectors | Staging only, `eks-staging-us-west-2`, ~114 repos, single replica |
| **entire-graph** | Us | Go | Structural code graph: typed symbols + 30 relation types, ranked search, impact, diff | Tree-sitter snapshot, tree-hash-keyed cache. No vectors | One-shot local binary, plus brain ingestion |
| **entire-search** | Alisha | - | Product-entity search over transcript chunks, commits, PRs. Deliberately strips code | Cohere embed-v4, 1536-dim, Turbopuffer | Yes, serves entire.io |
| **librarian** | Alex | - | Comms and docs knowledge. No code | nomic-768, pgvector | Yes |

entire-search and librarian are prior verified context. Neither is code search, neither overlaps
here, and neither is touched by this RFD.

### Duplicate 1: two tree-sitter extractor stacks

peregrine ships 15 per-language extractors plus import resolvers (`src/symbols/mod.rs:8-22`,
`:25-39`). entire-graph ships a semantic path for **36** languages (`docs/language-support.md`),
a strict superset: all 15 of peregrine's tier-1 languages appear in it. Two teams pay grammar
maintenance and upgrade churn for an overlapping set, and the smaller stack is the one users hit.

The duplication already costs coverage, not just effort. **peregrine's Kotlin support does not
work.** `src/symbols/parser.rs:15-34` wires only 14 grammars; Kotlin is absent with the comment
"tree-sitter-kotlin 0.3.x links against tree-sitter 0.20 (incompatible with 0.26)" (`:27`).
Unmapped languages return `None` (`:6-11`) and `extract_symbols` returns empty
(`extract.rs:93-96`), so `lang_kotlin.rs` is unreachable and every Kotlin file yields zero
symbols, despite the README advertising Kotlin as tier 1. entire-graph extracts Kotlin today.

Precision is the larger gap, and peregrine's source says so. It has **two** resolvers:

- **Index-time, persisted, crude.** `batch_resolve_references` (`src/symbols/resolve.rs:122-179`)
  populates `resolved_to` in every shipped index (called from `src/index/writer.rs:170`, `:416`,
  `src/index/incremental.rs:1121`). Its own comment: "ponytail: uses simple name-matching +
  same-directory preference heuristic" (`resolve.rs:118`). Repo-wide `name -> defs` map, prefer a
  same-directory candidate, else **pick the first arbitrarily** (`:174-176`). No import parsing,
  no qualifier or type awareness.
- **Query-time, not persisted, better.** `resolve_file_references` (`:185-380`) parses imports,
  filters external packages and disambiguates by qualifier, but runs one file per request behind
  `POST /api/resolve` (`src/server/http.rs:1296`), recomputed every call.

`README.md` describes only the second and claims resolution is "query-time, not index-time,"
which is misleading about what ships in the index. The honest statement: peregrine's persisted
resolution is name-based and heuristic with arbitrary tiebreaks. Its wanted upgrade is documented
as expensive at build time (`resolve.rs:119-121`), and is exactly the work entire-graph already
does elsewhere.

### Duplicate 2: entire-graph is starting to build a search engine

Branch `codex/eg-graphify-lexical-sidecar` (commit `5442ed87`, not on main, divergent) adds a real
**trigram-postings on-disk lexical index**: `internal/sem/search_lexical_index.go` (984 lines)
plus `search_source_pack.go` (455 lines), magic headers `EGLEXI1` / `EGPOST1` (`:35-36`),
artifacts `manifest.json` / `lexicon.bin` / `postings.bin` (`:26-28`). Confirmed dormant, zero
callers in the query path. That is a second trigram engine, in a second language, inside the repo
whose own boundary doc says serving is not its job. This RFD is the decision that closes it.

### Duplicate 3: no single code-search front door

peregrine is reachable through the entire-api gateway as upstream `"peregrine"`
(`entire-api/internal/server/api.go:399`), spec-merged under a `/search` prefix (`:451-457`), and
surfaced to agents as `search_entire_code` (`mcp/internal/entiremcp/curatedtools.go:619-666`).
entire-graph reaches agents by a disjoint route: a shell-out binary and brain ingestion.
`grep -rni "entire-graph"` across the MCP repo returns **zero hits**. Callers pick a door by
accident, and the two doors disagree about what a symbol is.

### The seam already exists, and was designed on purpose

peregrine reserved an external precision producer from the start: `src/symbols/types.rs:111-115`
`enum SymbolSource { TreeSitter = 0, Scip = 1 }`, `:118-122`
`enum SymbolPrecision { Syntax = 0, Semantic = 1 }`, `:137-138` both carried on every `Symbol`,
`:265-276` `deserialize` already mapping byte `1` to `Scip` and `Semantic`. Deliberately, per its
own spec: "source and precision fields exist to support future SCIP overlay without schema
changes" and "Resolution ... is explicitly out of scope for v1 (requires import analysis or SCIP)"
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-31-symbolic-search-design.md:45,48`), with `docs/design.md:27`
recording "SCIP evaluated later." Nothing constructs `SymbolSource::Scip` today. It is a reserved
slot waiting for a producer.

The producer exists but is **not merged**: PR #97 (`ec/candidate-scip-export-v2`, ashtom, OPEN,
`CONFLICTING` with main, 0 reviews) adds `snapshot --format scip` emitting a real `scippb.Index`
via `github.com/scip-code/scip/bindings/go/scip v0.9.0`, deterministically marshalled
(`internal/sem/compact_snapshot.go:454,462`), with unsupported relations reported in a JSON stderr
omission note.

## Options considered

### Option A: peregrine absorbs entire-graph's extraction via a SCIP feed

One extractor, two engines. entire-graph produces SCIP per `repo@commit`; peregrine ingests it
into `.pg` section 6 as `Scip` / `Semantic`, keeping its native layer as fallback. Cons:

- Adds a cross-repo build dependency and a new failure mode, a stale or absent feed. Needs an
  explicit freshness contract and fallback or quality silently regresses.
- **SCIP is a lossy projection.** Only 15 of entire-graph's 30 relation types map to SCIP
  references (`compact_snapshot.go:540-547`); the rest drop into `UnsupportedRelationCounts`
  (`:427-429`). Only `Import`, `WriteAccess`, `ReadAccess` get explicit roles (`:549-560`); CALLS,
  EXTENDS, IMPLEMENTS emit role 0. entire-graph cannot retire its native snapshot format.
- **The monikers are not portable.** The exporter hardcodes scheme `"entire-graph"`, package
  manager `"."`, package name = repo key (`:660-664`), and embeds `shortDigest(record.ID)`, an
  internal ID, in the descriptor (`:613-636`). Syntactically valid SCIP carrying
  entire-graph-specific identity, not monikers another indexer resolves to the same symbol.
- PR #97 "materializes one complete SCIP index in memory before writing it," an unvalidated scale
  risk on a monorepo. It also couples release cadences: peregrine's build waits on an
  entire-graph run.

### Option B: entire-graph becomes the search engine too

Delete peregrine, serve everything from entire-graph. Cons, close to disqualifying:

- It contradicts a boundary already ratified in this repo. `docs/brain-and-graph-boundaries.md`
  declares the MCP server surface "Brain's job" and multi-repo / cross-project graph "Brain's
  job," because "there is no equivalent identity for 'nine repositories as of roughly now'." Code
  search is inherently multi-repo fan-out.
- entire-graph is a one-shot, no-egress binary, not a serving system. Caches key on the git

  one-character change alters the tree hash and forces a full rebuild. Per-file invalidation is
  "unbuilt, not declined" per the boundary doc.
- It discards a working, benchmarked engine. peregrine indexes are roughly 4.9x smaller than
  Zoekt's with about 4x faster exact search (README), it does `git diff-tree` incremental indexing
  with surgical section splices (`src/index/patch.rs:1-6`), and it is already wired through the
  gateway and MCP. Rebuilding trigram search, regex literal pruning, mmap serving and an anon
  gate in Go is quarters of work to reach parity we already have.

### Option C: status quo plus contracts

Keep both extractors, write a compatibility contract, let each engine serve its own door. Cons:

- It removes nothing, so it does not satisfy COR-786. Maintenance cost is unchanged and grows with
  every grammar bump. Kotlin stays broken in peregrine.
- The stacks keep drifting on symbol identity, and a contract with no shared producer has no
  enforcement point. Callers still have to know which door to knock on.
- Its single honest advantage is that it carries no migration risk.

## Decision: Option A

**entire-graph becomes the precision symbol producer. peregrine remains the serving engine and the
single front door.** This is the only option where each system keeps the half it is demonstrably
good at and drops the half it duplicates:

- peregrine is a serving system with a deployed footprint, incremental indexing, and an in-source
  admission that its persisted resolution is an arbitrary-tiebreak heuristic. It should stop
  owning symbol precision.
- entire-graph is a deterministic producer with 36 semantic languages, a frozen `1.x` schema
  contract (`docs/adr/0001-ga-schema-contract.md`), and an explicit written boundary against
  becoming a server. It should stop growing a serving surface and sell its precision to the engine
  that already serves.

Neither engine is deleted. The **duplicate halves** are.

### The interface

**Artifact.** One SCIP protobuf index per `repo@commit` from `entire-graph snapshot --format scip`
(PR #97), plus its JSON omission note as a required sidecar. The note is contract, not debug
output: it declares which relations and languages were skipped, which is what lets peregrine
decide per-language whether to trust the feed.

**Identity, and an addressing mismatch to resolve.** peregrine's `.pg` header carries `org_id`,
`repo_name`, `repo_id` and `indexed_commit: [u8; 20]` (`src/index/format.rs:33-44`), so the join
key exists consumer-side. But the **S3 object is repo-scoped, not commit-scoped**: key
`{repo_id[0..2]}/{repo_id}.pg` (`src/server/s3_store.rs:14-24`), overwritten on every rebuild
(`src/server/index_manager.rs:704-716`). There is no commit-addressed index history, and
entire-graph dedupes on tree hash rather than commit. The contract: the feed is addressed by
`(repo_id, commit_sha)`, the producer may dedupe by tree hash underneath, and the consumer
validates the feed against the `indexed_commit` it is currently building. The feed store is
commit-versioned even though the `.pg` store is not.

**Delivery.** The artifact lands in the same object store as the `.pg` index, written by the
producer and read by the indexer tier (`deploy/fleet/apps/peregrine/base/index-deployment.yaml`)
at build time. peregrine then writes `SectionType::SymbolTable = 6` (`src/index/format.rs:24-31`)
from the feed instead of from its own extractors. **No `.pg` version bump is required**: `VERSION`
stays `1` (`:6`), the enum values are already defined and parsed, and TOC sections are
independently addressable and CRC32-checksummed (`:52-58`), so section 6 can be rewritten alone.

**Freshness contract.**
1. A feed is valid only for the exact `indexed_commit` being built. Any other commit is ignored,
   never approximated. Staleness is a hard miss.
2. Per-language trust is driven by the omission note. A language reported skipped or degraded
   falls back for that language only, not for the whole index.
3. Relation loss is expected and bounded: the feed supplies **symbols and resolution**, not
   relations. entire-graph's native snapshot stays the source of truth for the graph.
4. The feed is advisory to availability. peregrine must build a complete, servable index with the
   feed entirely absent.

**Fallback.** peregrine's native tree-sitter layer is retained and stays the default when no valid
feed is present, emitting `TreeSitter` / `Syntax` exactly as today. `precision` becomes a queryable
field, so callers needing semantic guarantees can filter on it, and mixed-precision indexes are
legal and honest rather than hidden.

### Migration steps and owners

| # | Step | Owner | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rebase and merge PR #97, promote `--format scip` from experimental, freeze the omission-note schema | Us | Byte-identical export on repeat runs, already shown in PR #97 |
| 2 | Publish per-language SCIP coverage matrix vs peregrine's tier-1 15 | Us | Reviewed by Evis |
| 3 | Decide the moniker scheme (open question 2) | Us + Evis | Written into the contract |
| 4 | Build the parity harness | TBD (open question 5) | Reproducible by both sides |
| 5 | Add SCIP ingestion to peregrine's index writer, per-repo flag, default off | Evis | Feed-off path byte-identical to today |
| 6 | Run parity on N repos, feed-on vs feed-off | Joint | Recall no worse, precision better, budgets held |
| 7 | Flip default to feed-on per language as each clears parity | Evis | Per-language, reversible |
| 8 | Wire the converged surface into the single MCP front door | Us + Alisha | Follows the `brain_*` plane pattern, P2.M3 |
| 9 | Remove peregrine's duplicate extractors at feed-on parity | Evis | Two release cycles feed-on, no rollback |

### What "deprecate duplicates" concretely removes, and when

Nothing is removed before step 7 has held for two release cycles. Then:

- **peregrine**: the per-language extractors and import resolvers (`src/symbols/lang_*.rs`,
  `src/symbols/imports_*.rs`) for every language at feed-on parity, plus the index-time heuristic
  `batch_resolve_references` (`resolve.rs:122`) once no shipped language depends on it. Up to 15
  extractor modules and 15 import-resolver modules, including `lang_kotlin.rs`, dead today.
  tree-sitter stays only for languages still on the fallback path. `resolve_file_references` stays
  as the query-time path for repos with no feed.
- **entire-graph**: branches `codex/eg-graphify-lexical-sidecar` and
  `codex/eg-graphify-query-service` are closed rather than merged.
  `docs/brain-and-graph-boundaries.md` gains a verdict entry recording that full-text and
  multi-repo code search is peregrine's job. entire-graph's own `search` stays, scoped to
  single-repo structural ranking, as `docs/search.md` already describes.
- **Front door**: `search_entire_code` becomes the one code-search tool. Its dropped `usages` mode
  should be reinstated: the MCP ADR recorded "peregrine has no such endpoint today"
  (`docs/adrs/20260721-mcp-curated-product-surface.md:145`), now stale, since `/api/usages` exists
  at `peregrine/src/server/http.rs:1688` and entire-api allowlists `/search/api/usages` (`:458`).

### Test and rollout gates

- **Corpus**: at least 10 repos spanning all peregrine tier-1 languages, including one monorepo
  large enough to test PR #97's in-memory materialization.
- **Primary metric**: symbol recall and precision of the SCIP-fed symbol table against peregrine's
  native layer, per language, definitions and references scored separately. Cross-file
  `resolved_to` correctness scored against hand-labelled ground truth, since that is the field the
  heuristic is weakest on and the one a semantic producer should most improve.
- **Non-regression**: recall must not drop in any language. A precision gain that costs recall is
  a fail, because users notice a missing hit more than a spurious one.
- **Budgets**: `.pg` size delta, index build wall-clock delta, p50/p99 query latency, each with a
  ceiling agreed with Evis before the run, not after.
- **Rollout**: per-repo flag, then per-language default, then global, each stage reversible by
  clearing the flag and falling back to the native layer with no reindex. Feed-off stays a
  permanently supported configuration, not a transitional state.

### Non-goals

- **Embedding backbone convergence.** Cohere embed-v4/Turbopuffer versus nomic-768/pgvector is
  COR-788, separate RFD. Nothing here adds vectors; both engines in scope are non-vector and stay
  that way.
- **Prose and knowledge search.** entire-search and librarian keep their corpora and owners.

## Open questions

1. **SCIP coverage per language.** 36 semantic languages against peregrine's 15, but the
   projection is lossier than the native snapshot and its per-language fidelity is unmeasured.
   Step 2 answers this and could shrink the set that ever reaches feed-on. Doc drift to reconcile:
   `docs/language-support.md` says 185 supported / 36 semantic, live `capabilities --json` says
   179 / 35.
2. **Symbol identity.** The exporter emits entire-graph-internal identity inside SCIP syntax
   (`compact_snapshot.go:613-636,660-664`). peregrine joins on name plus position today, so the
   initial feed works, but this blocks cross-repo and cross-tool navigation later. Real
   package-manager monikers now, or internal IDs and revisit? Decide before step 5.
3. **Index size and latency budgets.** Semantic symbols carry more data per symbol. peregrine's
   headline is 4.9x smaller than Zoekt; decide how much of that lead is for sale before spending it.
4. **In-memory materialization.** PR #97 builds the full SCIP index in memory. Unknown whether that
   survives our largest monorepo. Measure before step 5.
5. **Who owns the parity harness?** It must be trusted by both sides, which argues against either
   side owning it alone. Unassigned, and the biggest scheduling risk here.
6. **Producer runtime placement.** Inside peregrine's indexer tier, or a separate job publishing to
   the object store? Affects failure isolation and paging.
7. **Feed store addressing.** The `.pg` store is repo-keyed and overwritten in place while the feed
   is commit-keyed. Commit-versioned feed store with its own retention, or repo-keyed and accept
   that a rebuild races the feed?
8. **Staging to production.** peregrine is staging-only, single replica, no live autoscaling per
   `docs/go-live-plan.md`, no production cluster overlay in the repo. Convergence assumes it
   reaches production. If that slips, COR-786 lands on an engine no user can reach.

## Consequences

- One tree-sitter extraction stack of record, maintained by one team, covering a superset of
  today's languages, and fixing Kotlin as a side effect.
- Symbol precision becomes an explicit queryable property rather than an undocumented heuristic.
- peregrine gains a cross-repo build dependency it did not have, mitigated by a mandatory
  always-supported fallback.
- entire-graph gains a second consumer contract alongside brain. ADR 0001's additive-only `1.x`
  rules should extend to the SCIP projection and its omission note.
- COR-786 closes when steps 1 through 7 land and step 9 removes the first duplicate extractor.
  Step 8 continues into P2.M3.

It's straightforward to *merge* — one file, no code, no tests. It is not straightforward in what merging it means. Two concrete problems, then my actual read.

## 1. Blocking: the ADR number is already taken

## Evidence status

The former 54.9% Haiku, 57.7% Sonnet, and 31–73% open-model token-savings
figures are withdrawn. They were token-first measurements under a prompt policy
that encouraged the graph arms to stop early and did not require equivalent
resolution evidence from every arm. “Patch produced” was also reported as task
completion, which is not the same as passing the task's tests.

A replacement claim requires:

- identical tool-agnostic working instructions across arms;
- each tool's normal interface;
- official task resolution as the primary outcome;
- token and turn comparisons over commonly resolved tasks;
- repeated runs with uncertainty; and
- pinned binaries, prompts, datasets, and retained raw artifacts.

## More

### Compact and SCIP snapshot artifacts

`entire graph snapshot --repo . --format ndjson` remains the interoperable default: it is the existing object-per-line stream. For a complete, local compact artifact, use:

```sh
entire graph snapshot --repo . --format compact-ndjson > graph.compact.ndjson
entire graph snapshot-query --input graph.compact.ndjson --symbol Cache.Refresh --format ndjson
entire graph snapshot-query --input graph.compact.ndjson --from '<stable-id>' --relation CALLS --format ndjson
```

Compact NDJSON v1 is full-snapshot-only; targeted `--to`, `--from`, and `--relation` output stays native NDJSON. Its first `h` line is the only version marker, dictionary `d` lines are part of the artifact and its raw byte count, and unknown versions are rejected. The compact and native streams must have the same decoded public projection and canonical semantic SHA-256; hash equality alone is not a losslessness proof. Compact cache entries use a separate namespace from native snapshot entries.

For experimental SCIP consumers, write the protobuf index to a binary file and keep stderr for the machine-readable omission note:

```sh
entire graph snapshot --repo . --format scip > index.scip 2> index.scip.omissions.json
```

The SCIP export is complete-snapshot-only and never changes the default NDJSON stream. It emits definitions and supported reference-like relations as line-granular SCIP occurrences; relation families that do not map to SCIP references are omitted from the protobuf and counted in the stderr JSON note. A `--worktree` export uses `worktree` rather than the current commit as its SCIP package version and records `worktree_snapshot: true` in that note. Because a SCIP `Index` is one protobuf message, this experimental path assembles the complete index in memory. `--progress` is rejected so stderr remains exactly one parseable JSON note.

1. exactly one header line (a record with `schema_version`),
2. `file` records, then `symbol` records (emitted per file as parsing
   progresses, before any relation is resolved),
3. `relation` records and the `external` endpoint records they reference,
4. exactly one trailing `summary` record (`record_type: "summary"`).

**The first header is intentionally lean.** It carries identity (`provider`,
`provider_version`, `repo_root`, `repo_key`, `commit`, `tree`), `schema_version`,
`capabilities`, `schema_features`, `language_versions`, and the **profile
metadata** — `profile`, `profile_limits`, `relation_set`, and
`skipped_relation_families`. Its `languages`, `warnings`, `partial_failures`,
`stats`, and `completeness` are empty/zero — those totals are not known until
the whole repository has been processed, and the header is emitted before that
so consumers can begin work immediately. The profile metadata is **header-only**:
it is known up front and is therefore not repeated in the summary.

**The final `summary` record is authoritative for aggregate metadata.** It
carries the real `languages`, `warnings`, `partial_failures`, `stats` (including
the `relations` count and `completeness_level`), and the `completeness`
breakdown. It does **not** carry profile metadata (`profile`, `profile_limits`,
`relation_set`, `skipped_relation_families`); consumers should read those from
the lean header and must not expect them in the summary unless a future schema
version adds them.

**Merging the two.** A consumer that wants one fully-populated header should
take the lean header and overlay the summary's aggregate fields (`languages`,
`warnings`, `partial_failures`, `stats`, `completeness`) on top of it — summary
wins for any field both records carry, the header wins for the profile metadata
the summary omits. The in-memory `BuildProviderSnapshot` path does exactly this
merge internally, so its single emitted header is fully populated. For any
aggregate total, read the summary, never the lean header.

### Compact snapshot NDJSON v1

`snapshot --format ndjson` remains the default interoperable object stream. `snapshot --format compact-ndjson` is a public, full-snapshot-only artifact with a separate cache mode, `snapshot:compact-ndjson-v1`; it is rejected for `symbols`, `edges`, and targeted `--to`/`--from`/`--relation` output. Its first line is `["h", 1, header]`, and the version appears nowhere else. Deterministic first-seen dictionary lines `d` precede positional `f` (file), `x` (external), `s` (symbol), and `r` (relation) rows; a trailing `m` summary is mandatory. Consumers must reject unknown versions, malformed row arity, non-first or duplicate headers, and missing summaries.

All `h`, `d`, data, and `m` bytes count as raw compact artifact bytes; dictionary overhead must never be subtracted. Compact output is loaded only through the production compact loader and queried with `snapshot-query --input <file> --symbol <id-or-name> [--from <stable-id> --relation <TYPE>] --format ndjson`, which writes deterministically ordered native symbol/relation records. Its decoded public projection and canonical semantic SHA-256 (normalized native records in record order) must equal the normal NDJSON snapshot. Matching only the hash is not sufficient evidence of losslessness.

### Experimental SCIP snapshot protobuf

`snapshot --format scip` is an experimental, complete-snapshot-only projection for SCIP consumers. It writes a single binary SCIP `Index` protobuf to stdout and a single JSON omission note to stderr. It is rejected for `symbols`, `edges`, targeted `--to`/`--from`/`--relation` output, and `--progress`, and it is not served from the NDJSON or compact snapshot caches. A `--worktree` export uses `worktree` instead of the current commit as its SCIP package version, includes `--worktree` in `ToolInfo.arguments`, and sets `worktree_snapshot: true` in the note. If the underlying snapshot is partial, the same stderr JSON object includes `partial_snapshot`, `completeness_level`, `warning_count`, and `partial_failure_count` instead of mixing human warning text into stderr. Unlike the NDJSON encoders, the SCIP encoder retains the complete graph until it can write the one protobuf message, so its memory use scales with snapshot size.

The protobuf contains `Metadata`, one `Document` per source path, `SymbolInformation` for native symbol definitions, definition occurrences, and reference occurrences for supported reference-like relations: `IMPORTS`, `CALLS`, `CONSTRUCTS`, `ASYNC_CALLS`, `EXTENDS`, `INHERITS`, `IMPLEMENTS`, `OVERRIDES`, `USES_TYPE`, `PARAM_TYPE`, `RETURNS_TYPE`, `READS_FIELD`, `WRITES_FIELD`, and `ACCESSES`. Occurrence ranges cover the complete one-based inclusive line spans supplied by Entire Graph; the export does not invent unavailable columns. Native `DEFINES` and `CONTAINS` relations are represented by symbol metadata and definition occurrences rather than emitted as relation edges. Other relation families are omitted from the SCIP protobuf and counted by relation type in the stderr note:

```json
{"record_type":"scip_omissions","version":"entire-graph-scip-omissions/v1","format":"scip","unsupported_relation_counts":{"DATA_FLOWS":1},"missing_target_relations":0,"missing_evidence_relations":0,"emitted_definitions":2,"emitted_references":1}
```

The native NDJSON stream remains the lossless provider contract. The SCIP export is an interoperability artifact for navigation tools whose model is definitions and references, so consumers that need full Entire Graph relation semantics must keep using `--format ndjson` or `--format compact-ndjson`.

### Process-local cold-build telemetry

The optional provider progress callback exposes only process-local performance
telemetry. Its typed phases are `inventory` (source preparation/file discovery),
`parse` (header output, registration aliases, file/symbol output, and index
construction), `relations` (relation resolution), and `finalize` (external
output plus trailing-summary construction and serialization). Each event carries
both elapsed time since that phase began and total provider-work time since
snapshot entry. Progress sampling and the synchronous caller callback are
measurement overhead and are excluded from both durations; the next phase clock
starts only after the prior terminal callback returns. The final event is sent
after the trailing summary has been emitted. These telemetry fields are not
snapshot schema fields and must never alter emitted semantic records.

**Ordering.** For a fixed input and profile the stream is deterministic and
stable (file, symbol, and relation order are reproducible across runs), but it
is not globally sorted the way the in-memory path sorts relations. Consumers
should key on record `id`/identity, not on stream position.

**Unknown record types.** Consumers must ignore record types they do not
recognize within a supported major schema version (forward compatibility for new
record types), and must not assume every line is a known type. A consumer that
reads only the header and relations, for example, should skip `file`, `symbol`,
`external`, and `summary` lines it does not need rather than erroring on them.

**PR 97 is mergeable.** `CONFLICTING` → `MERGEABLE`, 248 behind → **0 behind**, pushed `831657e1..cbf9399d` as a fast-forward with both parents preserved.

## The five conflicts

**Two mechanical:**
- `go.mod` / `go.sum` — additive on both sides (branch: scip + protobuf + beaut; main: x/sys + x/text). Unioned, then `go mod tidy`.

**Three that needed judgment:**

- **`internal/cli/root.go`** — main had refactored the snapshot cache around both of the branch's edits. I took main's `var commit, tree string` + `cacheContext := ctx` while keeping the branch's `&& !scip`, and moved the store guard to main's `if recordsCache != nil` with the SCIP omission-note branch in front. Before committing I verified the `&& !scip` still does its job: `recordsCache` is only constructed inside `if useCache`, so excluding SCIP means no cache transaction is ever begun for a SCIP export.

- **`README.md`** — main moved format docs out of the README entirely. Re-adding the branch's "Compact and SCIP snapshot artifacts" block would have reintroduced content main deliberately relocated. Took main's side; the README no longer documents `compact-ndjson` either, so dropping SCIP from it is consistent.

- **`docs/semantic-provider-requirements.md`** — main replaced the inline spec with a pointer to the new canonical `docs/snapshot-format.md`. I preserved the branch's "Experimental SCIP snapshot protobuf" section and **moved it there**, promoted to `##` and placed right after "Compact snapshot NDJSON v1", its sibling format. `docs/commands.md` now lists `--format scip` in the snapshot row.

Rename detection carried the branch's `docs/DETAILS.md` edits into `docs/archive/2026-08-12-legacy-details.md` — a file whose own header reads *"Archived… superseded… duplicates the root README and contains stale claims."* Git was correct that it's the same file; documenting a brand-new format in an explicitly non-normative archive is not. content.text:
Review complete.

## Verdict: **Advisory** — the export is well-built; one design consequence needs a decision before it feeds anything

No correctness defects. Determinism, error handling, line ranges, and the schema contract all check out. The findings are about *identity semantics*, which matter because RFD 0005 makes this a feed.

---

## Findings

### 1. **Advisory (design)** — Monikers embed the commit, so symbol identity churns completely every commit

`compact_snapshot.go`, `scipSymbolPackage`: the SCIP package version is `header.Commit`. Real output from my smoke repo:

```
entire-graph . local/scip-demo d26959da4faa… `a.go`/Helper(s6c2d1de57f6f).
```

I tested what that means. Same repo, `a.go` **byte-identical**, one unrelated commit added:

```
commit 1:  entire-graph . local/scip-demo d26959da4faa… `a.go`/Helper(s6c2d1de57f6f).
commit 2:  entire-graph . local/scip-demo 3ec3b1482832… `a.go`/Helper(s6c2d1de57f6f).
```

The two indexes share **zero** symbol strings. The RFD's open question 2 frames this as blocking *cross-repo and cross-tool* navigation later. It also blocks **cross-commit** navigation now, which is more immediate for a per-`repo@commit` feed: a consumer keying on the full moniker sees 100% churn on every commit.

The mitigation is already in the data — the descriptor tail `Helper(s6c2d1de57f6f)` **is** stable, because `shortDigest` hashes the `compound-v1` ID that AGENTS.md guarantees stable across ordinary edits. So a consumer can join on the descriptor and ignore the package version. That works, but it means the moniker is not a stable identity as a whole, only its suffix is — and that's not how SCIP monikers are meant to be consumed. Worth deciding before peregrine ingests, not after.

### 2. **Low** — In-memory materialization costs ~1.5×, now measured

RFD open question 4 asks whether this survives a monorepo. On entire-graph itself (28 MB of NDJSON), `--no-cache`, both orders:

| Format | Peak RSS |
|---|---|
| `ndjson` | 114–117 MB |
| `compact-ndjson` | 119 MB |
| **`scip`** | **167–173 MB** |

So ~1.5×, roughly +55 MB — a real but bounded overhead, not a 10× cliff. Still unproven on a monorepo, but the multiplier is now known rather than guessed.

### 3. **Low** — Records with an empty ID or path are dropped silently

`Encode` does `if typed.Path != ""` / `if typed.ID != ""` before storing files, externals and symbols. A record failing those is discarded with no counter and no partial-failure entry. AGENTS.md's contract says unparseable input "must surface as machine-readable partial failures, never silent drops." These are almost certainly unreachable (they'd be provider bugs), and the omission note already has a counter idiom that would fit. Cheap to close.

### 4. **Note, not a defect** — `_unknown` synthetic document

`documentFor` maps an empty file path to a document literally named `_unknown`, which a consumer would see as a source file. I checked a real export of this repo: **zero** occurrences, so it's a defensive path only.

---

## What's solid

- **Determinism** — `proto.MarshalOptions{Deterministic: true}` plus sorted documents, occurrences, symbols and externals. Verified byte-identical across repeat runs.
- **Line ranges** — correct 1-based→0-based conversion with an exclusive end covering whole lines, with a comment explaining why no columns are invented, plus sane guards.
- **Stream contract** — header-first, single-header, summary-last all enforced with distinct errors; short writes surface as `io.ErrShortWrite`.
- **Schema contract** — `Capabilities` gains one additive boolean, `scip_snapshot_experimental`. Consistent with ADR 0001's additive-only `1.x` rule (`SchemaVersion` stays `"1.1"`, which matches the `compact_snapshot_ndjson_v1` precedent).
- **The omission note is the best part.** On this repo: 9,770 definitions and 25,476 references emitted, against 9,350 unsupported relations (`DATA_FLOWS` 5,048, `SIMILAR_TO` 3,294, …), 1,938 missing-evidence and 125 missing-target. The lossiness is quantified rather than hidden — which is exactly what makes RFD 0005's per-language trust decision possible.

## Test coverage

14 SCIP/compact tests, all passing, covering escaping round-trips, canonical language names, standard kinds/descriptors, worktree and no-HEAD provenance, and short writes. `TestSCIPSymbolEscapingRoundTrips` even parses monikers back with `scippb.ParseSymbol`, so they're valid SCIP.

**Gap:** nothing pins moniker stability. One test hardcodes `"entire-graph . repo version "` as a literal, so finding 1 would not be caught by any test — the churn is invisible to the suite.

## Residual risks

- I reviewed the SCIP encoder, not the pre-existing compact-snapshot code it shares a file with.
- Monorepo memory still unmeasured; I measured a 28 MB-output repo.
- No independent second opinion (`cursor-agent` still unauthenticated).
- Windows/Linux not native; CI covers it, and there's nothing platform-specific here.
- Forward interaction: the omission note goes to **stderr** as JSON. Go's `encoding/json` escapes C0 but not C1 — which is exactly PR #135's subject. Not exploitable here (relation-type keys come from a fixed 30-value enum), but the two touch the same surface.

## Recommendation

Merge-ready as an experimental format. Before it becomes RFD 0005's feed, close finding 1 — either commit to descriptor-only joins and say so in the contract, or drop the commit from the package version. Findings 2–4 are small.

Validated. All three forms parse, and the parse output settles the design question:

```
version="d26959da…"  desc=[name:"a.go" suffix:Namespace  name:"Helper" disambiguator:"s6c2d1de57f6f" suffix:Method]
version=""           desc=[…same…]
version="0.0.0"      desc=[…same…]
```

Note where the digest lands: SCIP's **`disambiguator`** field — which is exactly the standard mechanism for separating same-named symbols. The descriptor is already modelling stable identity correctly. The package version is the only thing breaking it.

## Recommendation: drop the commit from the package version

Use a stable placeholder (`.`, which parses to an empty version), and keep commit provenance where it already lives — `Metadata`, the omission note, and `ToolInfo.Arguments`.

Four reasons:

**The commit is already carried out-of-band.** RFD 0005's own contract addresses the feed by `(repo_id, commit_sha)` and has peregrine validate it against the `indexed_commit` it's building. Peregrine's `.pg` header carries `indexed_commit: [u8; 20]`. Embedding the commit in all ~9,770 symbol strings duplicates what the envelope already guarantees, and pays for it with total identity churn.

**It's not what the field means.** SCIP's package version exists so index A referencing `foo@1.2.3` links to index B that indexed `foo@1.2.3`. A repo's own commit isn't a package version in that sense — it's provenance, and provenance has a home in `Metadata`.

**Nothing is lost.** Worktree-vs-committed provenance is already triply encoded: `worktree_snapshot` in the note, `--worktree` in `ToolInfo.Arguments`, and the `E_NO_GIT_HEAD` / `W_WORKTREE_SNAPSHOT` warning handling. Removing the commit from the moniker deletes no information.

**It's free right now and expensive later.** The format is experimental with zero consumers. Once peregrine ingests it, changing symbol identity is a breaking change requiring a reindex.

Concretely, one function:

```go
func scipSymbolPackage(header SnapshotHeader) string {
	packageName := scipFirstNonEmpty(header.RepoKey, "repository")
	// No package version: this index is scoped to a commit by its envelope
	// (feed addressing, Metadata, the omission note), and putting the commit
	// here would give every symbol a new identity on every commit.
	return "entire-graph . " + scipPackageComponent(packageName) + " . "
}
```

I'd use `.` over `0.0.0` — it honestly says "no meaningful package version" and matches the package-manager field, which is already `.`.

## Why not the alternative

Keeping the commit and documenting descriptor-only joins is the other option, and I'd avoid it. It makes every consumer implement a non-standard join, and — the deciding factor — a consumer that does the *standard* thing doesn't get an error, it gets 100% churn that looks like "every symbol changed." Silent wrongness beats loud wrongness only for the person who wrote the code.

## One caveat

With a stable version, two indexes of the same repo at different commits produce **colliding** symbol strings. That collision is the desired identity, and peregrine keys by `repo_id` + `indexed_commit`, so it's contained. But if any consumer ever merges indexes from multiple commits into one flat store without the envelope, they'd conflate them. That should be written into the contract as an explicit consumer obligation — the same place RFD 0005 already specifies the freshness rules.

```go
}
```

with `parsePackageJSONName` as a direct precedent for `parsePackageJSONVersion`, and a nested-`package.json` walk already in place. No new file-reading surface, no new no-egress exposure, no new dependency.

## What I'd build

**Root manifest → version, fallback `0`.** Order it by which manifests actually carry a version: `package.json`, `Cargo.toml` (`[package] version`), `pyproject.toml` (`[project] version` / `[tool.poetry] version`), `pom.xml` (`<version>`), `composer.json`. Anything unparseable or absent falls back to `0` — never fail an export over a version string.

## Three things to decide, and one to expect

**`0` will be the common case for Go.** `go.mod` carries a module path, not a version — Go takes versions from git tags. `tsconfig.json` and `setup.cfg` usually have none either. So this repo, and most Go repos, land on `0` regardless. That's fine, but it means the win shows up for JS/Rust/Python/Java repos, not uniformly.

**Keep it per-repo for now, not per-package.** SCIP's package is per-*symbol*, so a monorepo with `packages/a@1.2.3` and `packages/b@2.0.0` should strictly give its symbols different packages. But today `scipSymbolPackage` uses `RepoKey` as one package name for the whole repo, so going per-version-without-per-name would produce the incoherent "one package, many versions." I'd take the **root** manifest's version now and treat per-directory package identity as a separate change — it moves the package *name* too, which is a bigger contract decision and belongs with RFD 0005's moniker question.

**Version bumps churn monikers — and that's correct.** Every symbol's identity changes when you release 1.2.3 → 1.2.4. Unlike per-commit churn this is rare and semantically true: it *is* a different package version. Worth stating in the contract so peregrine expects it.

**Mid-version commits collide, which is the point.** Twenty commits at `1.2.3` produce identical monikers for unchanged symbols. That's the stability finding 1 was asking for.

## Suggested shape

```go
func scipSymbolPackage(header SnapshotHeader, projectVersion string) string {
	packageName := scipFirstNonEmpty(header.RepoKey, "repository")
	// The package version is the project's own version from its root manifest,
	// not the commit: a commit here would give every symbol a new identity on
	// every commit, defeating cross-index linking. Commit provenance lives in
	// Metadata and the omission note. "0" means no manifest declared one.
	version := scipFirstNonEmpty(projectVersion, "0")
	return "entire-graph . " + scipPackageComponent(packageName) + " " + scipPackageComponent(version) + " "
}
```

fix(sem): make the SCIP package version the project's, not the commit

The SCIP package version carried header.Commit, so a symbol's identity changed
on every commit. Measured on a two-commit fixture where a.go was byte-identical
between them: the two indexes shared no symbol string at all.

    commit 1:  entire-graph . local/demo d26959da4faa... `a.go`/Helper(s6c2d1de57f6f).
    commit 2:  entire-graph . local/demo 3ec3b1482832... `a.go`/Helper(s6c2d1de57f6f).

The descriptor is already stable -- the digest hashes the compound-v1 ID, which
is stable across ordinary edits, and SCIP parses it into the `disambiguator`
field that exists for exactly this -- so only the version broke identity. That
also defeats the reason the field exists: cross-index linking works by matching
`foo@1.2.3` in one index against foo's own index at 1.2.3, which a commit can
never satisfy.

Read the project's own version from the root manifest instead: package.json,
then Cargo.toml, then pyproject.toml's [project] or [tool.poetry] table, falling
back to "0". go.mod, tsconfig.json and setup.cfg are deliberately not consulted;
none carries the version of the project it describes, so Go repositories get "0",
which is honest rather than invented.

Read from the tree the snapshot describes. A committed-tree export reads the
manifest at HEAD, so a version bumped only in a dirty working tree cannot reach
an index that describes a commit; --worktree reads the working tree. Verified
end to end: with HEAD at 4.5.6 and the working tree at 9.9.9, the committed
export emits 4.5.6 and --worktree emits 9.9.9.

Parsing is deliberately conservative. TOML is matched as `key = "value"` inside
the named table and nothing else, because this repository carries no TOML
dependency and a guess would become part of every symbol's identity. A dynamic
version, an inline table, a malformed manifest, or any unrecognized shape yields
"not declared" and falls through. No manifest failure can fail an export.

Commit and worktree provenance are unaffected: they are carried by Metadata, by
--worktree in ToolInfo.arguments, and by worktree_snapshot in the omission note.
Two of those were already asserted by the provenance tests, which now check that
the version is *unchanged* by worktree-ness rather than that it becomes the
string "worktree" -- a stronger property, since a symbol should have one identity
whether it was indexed from a commit or from the working tree.

Consumers must now treat (repo, commit) as coming from the envelope rather than
from the symbol. Two indexes of the same repository at different commits share
symbol identities by design; merging them into one flat store without keeping
their commits distinct would conflate them. Documented in docs/snapshot-format.md.

Done — pushed `cbf9399d..159ad517`. (The PR API still reports the old head; it lags a few seconds.)

## Finding 1 is fixed, your way

The version now comes from the project's own manifest. Measured end-to-end on the same fixture that exposed the bug:

| Scenario | Emitted moniker |
|---|---|
| No manifest, commit A | `entire-graph . local/scip-demo 0 \`a.go\`/Helper(s6c2d1de57f6f).` |
| No manifest, commit B | **identical** |
| `package.json` at `4.5.6` | `… local/scip-demo 4.5.6 \`a.go\`/Helper(…).` |
| HEAD `4.5.6`, dirty tree `9.9.9` | **`4.5.6`** — the dirty bump does not leak |
| Same, `--worktree` | `9.9.9` |

That last pair is the property I was most worried about: a committed-tree export reads the manifest at `HEAD` via `gitutil.ShowFile`, so a version bumped only on disk can't get into an index that claims to describe a commit.

## What I built

**`internal/sem/scip_project_version.go`** — `ScipProjectVersion(read ManifestReader)`, trying `package.json` → `Cargo.toml` → `pyproject.toml` (`[project]`, then `[tool.poetry]`), falling back to `0`. `go.mod`, `tsconfig.json` and `setup.cfg` are deliberately excluded: none carries the version of the project it describes, so Go repos get `0` honestly rather than something invented.

The TOML parser is deliberately narrow — `key = "value"` inside the named table, nothing else. No TOML dependency exists here, and a guess would become part of every symbol's identity, so a dynamic version, inline table, or malformed manifest all yield "not declared" and fall through. **No manifest failure can fail an export.**

**Tests** — 15 new cases, including the regression test that reproduces the original cross-commit experiment, a version bump *correctly* changing identity, worktree and committed exports agreeing, table isolation (`[dependencies] version` ignored), comments, malformed JSON, PEP 621 vs Poetry, and `go.mod` not being consulted.

**Two existing tests changed meaning for the better.** The worktree/no-HEAD provenance tests asserted the version *becomes* `"worktree"`; they now assert it's **unchanged** by worktree-ness. That's the stronger property — one symbol, one identity, however it was indexed — and provenance was already covered by their `Metadata.arguments` and `worktree_snapshot` assertions.

**Docs** — `snapshot-format.md` and `AGENTS.md` updated, including the consumer obligation: `(repo, commit)` comes from the envelope now, so merging indexes from different commits into one flat store would conflate them.

## Gate

gofmt, vet, build, and `go test ./...` green across all 8 packages.

## Two things I'd flag

**I did not implement per-package versions.** A monorepo with `packages/a@1.2.3` and `packages/b@2.0.0` gets one version for the whole repo, because the package *name* is still the repo key — per-directory versions without per-directory names would give the incoherent "one package, many versions." That's RFD 0005's moniker question and a bigger contract decision; the code says so in a comment.

**This is a breaking change to an unmerged experimental format** — which is exactly why now was the moment. Once peregrine ingests it, changing symbol identity means a reindex.

Findings 2–4 from the review are still open (memory ~1.5×, silent empty-ID drops, `_unknown` doc). Want any of those?
Yes

All four findings are now closed. Pushed `159ad517..a45fb53f`.

## Findings 2–4

**Finding 3 — silent drops.** `Encode` discarded unkeyable records via `if typed.ID != ""`, leaving no trace. They're now counted as `unidentified_records`. This was the one touching a stated contract: AGENTS.md requires unparseable input to surface as machine-readable partial failure, "never silent drops."

**Finding 4 — `_unknown` document.** Symbols with no file path are still emitted (so they can be referenced) but now counted as `unlocated_symbols`, so a consumer knows they have no navigable definition location.

Both use `omitempty`, so a clean export is unchanged — verified against this repo, whose note still carries exactly its original eight keys:

```
       missing_target_relations, record_type, unsupported_relation_counts, version]

unlocated_symbols  present: False
```

**Finding 2 — memory.** Not fixable: a SCIP `Index` is one protobuf message and can't be streamed. What was wrong was the doc saying memory "scales with snapshot size" without a number. It now records the measurement — ~170 MB vs ~115 MB (`ndjson`) and ~119 MB (`compact-ndjson`), about **1.5×** — with the caveat that a multiplier measured here doesn't carry to a monorepo, where the absolute figure is what matters. Here's how each flag gets addressed, cheapest first.

## Flag 3 — no independent review of my changes

**This turned out to be the sharpest of the three, and it has a concrete fix.**

Every other PR this session had a trail, and its agent review earned its keep: it caught `tag.gpgSign` on 133 after I'd fixed only `commit.gpgsign`, and it caught my broken `e3610e50` commit within two minutes. **PR 97 has no trail**, so that reviewer has never looked at it — and everything from `cbf9399d` onward is mine.

```
entire trail create --branch ec/candidate-scip-export-v2 \
  --title "feat: add experimental SCIP snapshot export" --type feature
```

That gives the branch Entire Gates and an agent review over the SCIP encoder and my four commits. It's a write to your Entire project, so I'd want your go-ahead — but it's the single highest-value thing available, and it doesn't depend on anyone's schedule.

Second lever, complementary rather than redundant: `! cursor-agent login` and I run an outside review of the pinned diff. Different model, different blind spots.

What I'd *not* rely on: me re-reviewing my own work. I'll do an adversarial pass if you want, but I've now been wrong twice this session in exactly the way self-review doesn't catch — asserting something plausible without testing it (`-foo`, "peregrine isn't verifiable"). Both were caught by running the thing, or by another reviewer.

## Flag 1 — RFD 0005's open questions are stale

Mechanical, and I have the branch ready. Two edits:

- **Q4 (in-memory materialization)** — no longer open in the abstract. Replace with the measurement: ~1.5× on a 28 MB-NDJSON repo, still unmeasured at monorepo scale, which is the part that stays open.
- **Q2 (symbol identity)** — currently one question, now two halves with different status. The commit-in-the-version half is **closed** (fixed, with a regression test). What remains is the `entire-graph` scheme, the internal-ID digest in the descriptor, and per-package identity. Q2 should say so rather than implying the whole thing is unresolved.

I'd also add a line to Q1: the doc-drift half is already reconciled, which I confirmed earlier.

## Flag 2 — per-package versions

This one is **a decision, not a task**, and it shouldn't be coded until it's decided. The question:

> In a monorepo, does `packages/a` become its own SCIP package, or does the whole repository stay one package?

Today the package *name* is the repo key, so I could only make the version per-directory by producing "one package, many versions," which is incoherent. Doing it properly means the name moves too — and that changes every symbol's identity a second time.

My recommendation: **don't build it now.** It's the same class of change as the moniker scheme (Q2's remaining half), it changes identity for every symbol, and both should land together as one deliberate contract decision rather than two churns. The right home is RFD 0005's Q2, not this PR. The code already carries a comment saying exactly this.

---

**Suggested order:** create the trail first (it may surface things that change what the RFD should say), then update the RFD once, then decide per-package identity with the RFD rather than ahead of it.

Want me to create the trail and update the RFD?

content.text:
All four check out. The independent review earned its keep — including on my own code.

## Verified findings

**1. Windows `ProjectRoot` URI — confirmed, reproduced.** `scipProjectRoot` does `(&url.URL{Scheme:"file", Path: root}).String()`:

```
"/home/u/repo"          -> file:///home/u/repo          ✓
"C:\repo"               -> file://C:%5Crepo             ✗ backslash escaped, drive as authority
"\\server\share\repo"   -> file://%5C%5Cserver%5Cshare  ✗
```

A Windows consumer can't resolve `ProjectRoot`. Not caught by CI because the Windows job runs the tests, and no test asserts the URI shape.

**2. `LanguageTiers` discarded — confirmed.** `SnapshotSummary.LanguageTiers` exists and the NDJSON header carries it (`provider.go:851`), but the SCIP path drops it. Every discovered file becomes a SCIP document, so an inventory-only file is indistinguishable from a semantically parsed one. **This one matters most for RFD 0005** — its freshness contract says "per-language trust is driven by the omission note," and the note currently can't express which languages were only inventoried.

**3. `PartialFailures` reduced to a count — confirmed.** `SnapshotSummary.PartialFailures []PartialFailure` becomes `partial_failure_count int`. Paths, codes and details vanish. This is the larger version of the silent-drop finding I raised myself: I caught unkeyable records, and missed that the *pre-existing* failure records were already being flattened.

**4. Unbounded manifest read — confirmed, and it's mine.** `scipProjectVersion` uses `gitutil.ShowFile` / `os.ReadFile` with no cap, while `ShowFileLimited` and `ReadFileLimited` sit right there in the same package. A repo with a huge `package.json` can exhaust memory before the provider's blob caps apply.

That last one is the one to sit with. I reviewed "resource bounds" as an explicit dimension on three other PRs, then wrote an unbounded read two commits ago and didn't catch it in my own gate. It's exactly the failure mode self-review doesn't find, and it's why the trail was worth creating rather than merging on the strength of green CI and my own read.

## Where this leaves things

CI on `aac8a0a5`: 8 green, `test` on macOS/Windows still running. Gates is red on **approvals only** — the four findings don't block, but they're real.

Findings 1 and 4 are small and mechanical. Findings 2 and 3 are contract-shaped: both are about the omission note being the place a consumer learns what it didn't get, which is precisely the role RFD 0005 assigns it — and I just wrote the note's evolution rules without noticing either gap.

Want me to fix all four? I'd do 4 and 1 first (bounded reads, URI normalization with a Windows test), then 2 and 3 together since both extend the note — which, conveniently, the additive-within-`v1` rule I just documented explicitly permits.

content.text:
The re-review found **three new findings**, and the most important one is my fault.

## Fixed and pushed (`e3456da2..9edae1fa`)

**Revision provenance — my error.** When I took the commit out of the package version, I wrote in both the commit message and `docs/snapshot-format.md` that *"commit and worktree provenance are carried instead by `Metadata`."* The worktree half was true. **The commit half was not** — SCIP `Metadata` carries `ToolInfo`, `ProjectRoot` and a text encoding, and has no revision field at all:

```go
return &scippb.Metadata{ToolInfo: …, ProjectRoot: …, TextDocumentEncoding: …}
```

So the revision survived nowhere. Two committed exports of the same repo at the same project version were indistinguishable from the artifacts alone — precisely the conflation that *same commit* documented as a consumer obligation, while I believed provenance existed to prevent it. I asserted it without checking, exactly the failure mode I keep hitting.

Now carried as `commit` / `tree` in the note, once per index, empty for worktree exports. Verified: `commit: 811ae5a20b57c97f | tree: e9aa62624d41b573`. Full gate green.

## Two findings I have *not* acted on — both real, both bigger

**Implementation relationships are lost.** `scipRoles` maps only `IMPORTS`/`WRITES_FIELD`/`READS_FIELD`; `IMPLEMENTS`, `INHERITS`, `EXTENDS`, `OVERRIDES` all fall to `return 0` and become plain reference occurrences. SCIP expresses those through `SymbolInformation.relationships` with `is_implementation`, so **"Find Implementations" returns nothing** — and because those types count as "supported," the loss isn't reported in the note either. That last part makes it worse than a gap: the artifact claims fidelity it doesn't have.

**Definition occurrences span the whole body.** `scipOccurrenceFromLines(record.StartLine, record.EndLine, …)` for a definition covers the entire declaration *and body*, so it overlaps every call inside it. SCIP wants the definition occurrence on the declaration and the full span in `enclosing_range`. As-is, positional lookup inside any multi-line function is ambiguous.

Both are pre-existing in the original PR rather than from my changes, and both are real SCIP-semantics bugs that would surface as "navigation silently doesn't work" for a peregrine consumer.

## One stale-looking finding that is actually fixed

`LanguageTiers` still shows as current, but I verified the note really does carry it now (`'language_tiers' in note → True`, 36 languages classified). The reviewer's anchor just didn't re-evaluate. I'd rather tell you that than mark it resolved myself.

## Where I'd stop

The trail is now doing what I couldn't: three rounds, eight findings, and it has caught a false claim of mine, an unbounded read of mine, and two genuine SCIP-semantics bugs. That argues for one more round after these fixes rather than declaring done.

The two open findings are a real chunk of work — `SymbolInformation.relationships` plus reworking definition ranges — and they change the artifact's shape, which touches RFD 0005's step 1 "freeze the schema." **My recommendation: fix them, but as their own commit and with your nod first**, since this PR has now absorbed a lot of scope beyond "make it mergeable."

Want me to take them?
